text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger will receive up to three billion schillings from postal and telecoms monopoly PTA. Two billion schillings in tax revenues alone will result from the sale of a 25 percent stake in mobile phone unit Mobilkom to Italy's stet for 8.4 billion schillings in cash.

- President Thomas Klestil declined to comment in detail on allegations he was aware that Austrian authorities bowed to Iranian pressure not to prosecute suspected killers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989. Klestil at the time had a senior position in Austria's foreign ministry.
- European Union Commission expects Austria to be one of 13 EU members to fulfil the Maastricht criteria for Europe's single currency this year.
- Austrian Association of Industry insist the government should subsidise the country's export offensive.
- Ruling Social Democrats and their junior coalition partners, the conservative People's Party, are split about plans to introduce a road pricing system for trucks on Austrian motorways.
- A new takeover law will require acquiring companies to make an equal offer to all shareholders of the company they aim to buy.
DIE PRESSE
- A new draft telecommunications law, aimed at preparing the sector for planned liberalisation next year, should be ready by mid-May.
- Gold sales in Austria could fall if the European Union goes ahead with plans to abolish tax-exempt status of gold.
- Ski jumper Andreas Goldberger faces new allegations of cocaine abuse.
- Austrian industry sees slight improvement in Austria's economy.
KURIER
- New allegations of cocaine abuse have tarnished Andreas Goldberger's image.
- First Austrian troops to take part in international security force for Albania have left for the troubled Balkan nation.
- Pensions set to fall as Social Affairs Ministry looks into ways of reforming Austria's ailing pension system.
- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel expects NATO to extend a formal invitation to Austria to join during the alliance's summit in Madrid.
- Erich Hampel, currently chief executive of postal savings bank PSK, is poised to take over as chief executive at Creditanstalt-Bankverein on April 29.
- Austria's tourism board head Michael Hoeferer says the provinces' inability to cooperate hurts the country's tourism industry.
